digest.top_line: SMART-KEY: 2y LFS 65.1% (80% CI 54.9-73.5) with cisplatin-free induction → IMRT + pembro in stage III-IVB glottic/supraglottic SCC, vs 64.9% in RTOG 9111.
digest.tldr: Head-neck carried the day: IO and ADCs are moving into curative-intent RT pathways, but every readout is single-arm, interim or retrospective. KEYNOTE-412 ctDNA: mid-CRT clearance tracked EFS in HPV- LA HNSCC (P values only). Multi-site: RADIANT RT foundation model hit GTV Dice 83.52%, external OS C-index 0.73-0.79.

sites.intro: Four curative-intent readouts that add IO or an ADC around RT or surgery; none yet has a randomised efficacy comparison.

studies.name: GORTEC 2024-03 IDEAL
studies.tldr: Interim safety analysis in LA-HNSCC: no G4 AEs; G3 TEAEs in 6 pts with ADC+anti-PD-1 vs 2 pts with ADC alone (10 per arm).
details: 🔍 Randomized (1:1) phase II, 2 arms each evaluated independently (one-stage Fleming design, H0=30%)
🔍 106 pts planned; 49 randomized Oct 2025 to Apr 2026
🔍 First interim safety analysis after cycle 1 in the first 20 pts (10 per arm)

subdetails: Arm A: pucotenlimab 200 mg + becotatug vedotin 2.3 mg/kg Q3W ×3 → CRT → adjuvant pucotenlimab Q3W ×8
Arm B: becotatug vedotin alone Q3W ×3 → CRT
CRT: IMRT 70 Gy + concurrent cisplatin, both arms

details: 🔍 Primary endpoint: CR at 12 weeks post-CRT; no primary endpoint result in source

details.text: 📊 First interim safety analysis by arm

subdetails: Arm A: ALT increase + constipation, myalgia + ALT increase + hypertension, neutropenia, diabetes, diarrhea, hyponatremia
Arm B: peripheral arterial ischemia, fatigue

details: 📊 Post-induction ORR (RECIST 1.1) 71% of first 15 evaluable pts, pooled across arms, preliminary
⚠️ Safety is after cycle 1 only; no data on CRT delivery, cisplatin dose intensity or RT interruptions
⚠️ ORR not split by arm and not mature; 'encouraging' conclusion rests on 15 pts
⚠️ Population mixes p16+ and p16- oropharynx (19 p16+ of 31 OPC) with larynx, hypopharynx, oral cavity

verdict.rationale: Interim safety analysis of a randomized phase II after cycle 1 in 20 pts; arms not compared formally, primary endpoint (12-wk CR) not yet reported.
verdict.audience: LA-HNSCC (larynx, hypopharynx, oral cavity, p16+/p16- oropharynx), pre-CRT

studies.significance: The RT question is whether EGFR-ADC induction, with or without anti-PD-1, compromises delivery of IMRT 70 Gy + cisplatin; the source reports cycle-1 toxicity only, with no CRT compliance data. Arm A had more G3 TEAEs (6 vs 2 pts), including ALT increase and neutropenia, worth watching before cisplatin.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Randomized (1:1) phase II**, each arm evaluated independently by one-stage Fleming design (H0=30%). **106 pts planned**, 49 randomized to date; this is the first interim safety analysis after cycle 1 in the first 20 pts.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **LA-HNSCC** of larynx, hypopharynx, oral cavity and oropharynx, **p16- and p16+**. Most had oropharyngeal cancer (31 pts, including 19 p16+).

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Arm A: **pucotenlimab 200 mg + becotatug vedotin 2.3 mg/kg Q3W ×3**, then CRT, then adjuvant pucotenlimab Q3W ×8. Arm B: becotatug vedotin alone ×3, then CRT.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **IMRT 70 Gy with concurrent cisplatin** in both arms. Fractionation and target volumes not stated in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: CR at 12 weeks post-CRT.** Post-induction ORR per RECIST 1.1 also reported, preliminary.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **No G4 AEs** in either arm. 11 G3 TEAEs in 8 pts (**6 arm A, 2 arm B**). One arm B death post-gastrostomy after 1 ADC cycle, deemed unrelated.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Becotatug vedotin ± pucotenlimab was tested first in R/M HNSCC (Xue, Clin Cancer Res 2026); IDEAL moves it to induction before definitive CRT. No comparison against CRT alone, the current standard, is built into this design.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents LA-HNSCC across subsites, p16+ and p16- oropharynx, planned for cisplatin-based IMRT. Does not represent R/M disease or pts unfit for cisplatin.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: There is no CRT-alone control, so any CR rate is read against H0=30%, not against standard CRT. Mixing p16+ and p16- disease will skew CR rates according to case mix.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The safety profile after one cycle does not settle whether induction delays or dilutes cisplatin-RT. The arm-level 12-week CR data and CRT compliance will decide whether this design is worth a randomized test against CRT alone.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Both arms proceed to IMRT 70 Gy + concurrent cisplatin, so the read that matters is CRT deliverability after induction, which the source does not yet report. Primary endpoint is CR at 12 weeks post-CRT, a response measure driven by the RT course.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Adding pucotenlimab to becotatug vedotin induction doubled-plus the G3 TEAE count after cycle 1 (6 vs 2 pts), with ALT increase, neutropenia and diabetes in arm A. Pooled ORR 71% in 15 evaluable pts gives no arm-level signal yet to justify the IO add-on.

open_questions: Does ADC induction compromise cisplatin-IMRT delivery?
Does adding anti-PD-1 improve 12-week CR over ADC alone?
Benefit by p16 status in oropharynx

studies.name: Neoadjuvant NivoDP in high-grade salivary gland carcinoma
studies.tldr: MPR 60.9% and pCR 32.6% among 46 operated pts after 3 cycles nivolumab + docetaxel/cisplatin in node-positive high-grade SGC; 24-mo DFS 76.0%.
details: 🔍 Phase II, single-center, single-arm; N=50 analyzed of 55 enrolled
🔍 Treatment-naïve resectable high-grade SGC with clinically positive nodes; salivary duct carcinoma 74.0%
💊 Nivolumab 360 mg + docetaxel 60 mg/m2 + cisplatin 60 mg/m2 q3w × 3, then surgery + risk-adapted adjuvant RT
📊 ORR 52.0%; 92.0% reached surgery; R0 93.5% of operated pts
📊 MPR 60.9% (n=28) exceeded predefined MPR ≥50% threshold; pCR 32.6% (n=15)

details.text: 📊 Pathologic response by histology (best responders reported)

details: 📐 DFS MPR vs non-MPR: NR vs 24.2 mo, HR 0.19 (95% CI 0.05-0.71), p=0.013
📊 12-/24-mo DFS 89.0%/76.0%; 24-mo OS 91.2%; median f/u 16.2 mo from surgery
⚠️ 4 pts never reached surgery: 2 progression, 1 G3 pneumonitis, 1 withdrawal
⚠️ Adjuvant RT dose, volume and risk-adaptation criteria not reported in source
⚠️ MPR-vs-non-MPR DFS is a responder comparison, not evidence the regimen improves DFS

verdict.rationale: Single-arm, single-center phase II with a pathologic surrogate primary; 16.2-mo median follow-up and no randomized comparator vs upfront surgery + adjuvant RT.
verdict.audience: Resectable high-grade SGC, cN+, treatment-naïve; mostly salivary duct carcinoma

studies.significance: pCR 32.6% after neoadjuvant NivoDP raises the RT question the trial did not test: whether a pathologic responder still needs full adjuvant RT. Adjuvant RT was risk-adapted, but criteria, dose and volumes are not reported in source, so de-escalation after pCR remains untested.
studies.monday_clinic: In a treatment-naïve cN+ high-grade SGC (especially salivary duct carcinoma), this supports referral to a neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy trial before surgery; it does not inform node-negative, low-grade or recurrent disease.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Phase II, **single-center, single-arm**. 55 enrolled; 4 screen failures and 1 benign histology excluded, **50 analyzed**. Median follow-up **16.2 mo** (95% CI 12.0-20.1) from surgery.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Treatment-naïve resectable high-grade SGC with clinically positive nodes.** Median age 62, 88.0% male, ECOG 1 in 88.0%. Stage III/IVA/IVB 34.0%/64.0%/2.0%; salivary duct carcinoma 74.0%, adenocarcinoma 10.0%, mucoepidermoid 8.0%.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Nivolumab 360 mg + docetaxel 60 mg/m2 + cisplatin 60 mg/m2 q3w for **3 cycles**, then curative surgery.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Risk-adapted adjuvant RT** after surgery. Dose, fractionation, target volumes and the criteria for adapting RT are **not reported in source**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: MPR (≤10% viable tumor)**, with a predefined success threshold of MPR ≥50%. Also reported: ORR, R0, pCR, DFS, OS, safety.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Mostly G1-2 TRAEs; **6 G≥3 TRAEs**, all manageable, no treatment-related deaths. One G3 pneumonitis prevented surgery.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Upfront surgery + adjuvant RT is the standard for resectable high-grade SGC, and the source states **no neoadjuvant strategy is established**. Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy has moved into other resectable solid tumors; this is an early attempt to carry it into SGC.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents treatment-naïve resectable high-grade SGC with clinically positive nodes, mostly salivary duct carcinoma. Does not represent node-negative, low-grade, unresectable or recurrent/metastatic SGC.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: MPR-vs-non-MPR DFS compares responders with non-responders, so prognosis and treatment effect are confounded. Histology-level response rates rest on small subsets, and mucoepidermoid response is not reported. HER2/AR status, relevant in salivary duct carcinoma, is not reported.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: High MPR and pCR rates make neoadjuvant NivoDP a candidate for randomized testing against upfront surgery. Whether it lowers distant metastasis, the stated rationale, is **not settled** at 16.2 mo median follow-up.

studies.interpretation:
The case for neoadjuvant therapy in high-grade salivary gland carcinoma rests on a failure pattern, not a local one. Node-positive high-grade disease, salivary duct carcinoma above all, tends to relapse distantly despite resection and adjuvant RT. Locoregional therapy is already doing its job, and the open question is whether early systemic exposure changes the metastatic trajectory. This trial is the first structured attempt to answer that with chemoimmunotherapy, and its primary endpoint, pathologic response, is the right early readout for a feasibility question but the wrong one for the distant-control question that motivated it.

On its own terms the result is clean. The predefined MPR threshold was crossed, nearly every patient reached surgery, and R0 rates were high, so the regimen did not compromise resectability. The toxicity signal is modest, though one patient lost the operation to pneumonitis. That cost matters more in a disease where surgery is the curative backbone than in one with good salvage options.

The survival figures are harder to read. The DFS gap between MPR and non-MPR patients is large, but a responder analysis cannot separate a regimen that works from tumors that were biologically kinder to begin with. Without a randomized arm of upfront surgery and adjuvant RT, the 24-month DFS and OS cannot be credited to NivoDP. The follow-up is also shorter than the window in which distant failure in this disease usually declares itself. The histology table invites over-reading: the strongest pCR rates come from adenocarcinoma and poorly differentiated subsets that make up a small slice of the cohort. Salivary duct carcinoma, the subtype most clinicians will apply this to, had a more modest pCR. The source also gives no HER2 or androgen-receptor stratification, which in salivary duct carcinoma is the biology that already steers systemic therapy in the advanced setting.

For radiation oncologists the trial is silent where it might eventually matter most. Adjuvant RT was risk-adapted, but the source does not say how, at what dose, or to what volumes. A pCR rate near one in three raises the obvious de-escalation question: could a complete responder with clean margins be spared full-dose postoperative RT, or have its nodal volumes reduced? Nothing here licenses that, and since locoregional control is already good with standard therapy, any omission would need its own prospective test.

What would make this result wrong is a randomized trial showing similar distant-metastasis rates with upfront surgery. Until then it is a credible platform for that trial, and a reason to enroll eligible patients rather than adopt the regimen off protocol.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: pCR 32.6% raises an adjuvant RT de-escalation question this trial did not test. RT was risk-adapted, but criteria, dose and volumes are not reported in source, so postoperative RT planning after a pathologic responder remains unchanged.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: First prospective signal for neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in cN+ high-grade SGC: MPR 60.9% after 3 cycles NivoDP, with MPR tracking with DFS (HR 0.19). HER2/AR status is not reported, which limits integration with biomarker-directed therapy in salivary duct carcinoma.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Neoadjuvant NivoDP did not compromise resection: 92.0% reached surgery with R0 93.5%. Progression before surgery occurred in 2 pts and G3 pneumonitis cost 1 pt the operation, which is the window to watch.

open_questions: Does neoadjuvant NivoDP reduce distant metastasis vs upfront surgery?
Can adjuvant RT be de-escalated after pCR?
Response by HER2/AR status in salivary duct carcinoma

studies.name: SMART-KEY (LACOG 0720)
studies.tldr: 2y laryngectomy-free survival 65.1% (80% CI 54.9-73.5) with cisplatin-free induction, then IMRT plus pembrolizumab, in stage III-IVB glottic/supraglottic SCC.
details: 🔍 Single-arm, multicenter phase 2, N=43 across 9 centers, enrolled Feb 2022 to Aug 2023
🔍 Newly diagnosed stage III-IVB glottic/supraglottic SCC; 62.8% glottic, 83.7% former/current smokers
💊 Induction: carboplatin AUC6 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 + pembrolizumab 200 mg, three 21-day cycles
💊 Then IMRT with concurrent pembrolizumab alone (no concurrent chemo), then fourteen 21-day cycles of pembrolizumab consolidation
⚠️ RT dose, fractionation and target volumes not reported in source

details.text: 📊 2y outcomes vs historical controls (as tabulated by the investigators)

details: ⚠️ Efficacy reported with 80% CI, not 95%
⚠️ Rationale is lower late cisplatin/RT morbidity and mortality, which 2y data cannot yet show

verdict.rationale: Single-arm phase 2, N=43, 2y endpoint; benefit judged only against historical RTOG 9111 and GORTEC 2000-01 controls, with no randomized cisplatin-RT comparator.
verdict.audience: Newly diagnosed stage III-IVB glottic/supraglottic SCC

studies.significance: The concurrent phase drops cisplatin entirely, with IMRT given alongside pembrolizumab alone, yet 2y larynx preservation was 86% (RTOG 9111: 88%). Locoregional failure at 18.8% dominates over distant at 7.4%, so the RT backbone carries local control here. The dose and volumes are not in the source, which limits how well this carries over to your own fractionation.
studies.monday_clinic: In newly diagnosed stage III-IVB glottic or supraglottic SCC pursuing larynx preservation, this raises the question of whether concurrent cisplatin is needed only as trial context; it does not change care for cisplatin-eligible pts outside a trial or extend to other head-neck subsites.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Single-arm, multicenter phase 2**, N=43 from 9 centers, enrolled Feb 2022 to Aug 2023. Efficacy is compared with **historical controls** (RTOG 9111, GORTEC 2000-01), not a concurrent arm.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Newly diagnosed stage III-IVB glottic/supraglottic SCC.** Median age 61.1y, 86% male, 83.7% former/current smokers, 62.8% glottic.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Induction **carboplatin AUC6 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 + pembrolizumab 200 mg** for three 21-day cycles, then pembrolizumab during IMRT, then **fourteen 21-day cycles** of pembrolizumab consolidation. **Cisplatin-free throughout**, and no concurrent chemotherapy.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **IMRT with concurrent pembrolizumab alone.** Dose, fractionation and target volumes are **not reported in source**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: 2y laryngectomy-free survival.** Also reported: larynx preservation, larynx dysfunction-free survival, OS, and locoregional and distant recurrence.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **G≥3 TRAEs 41.9%**, including one G5. Immune-mediated G≥3 TRAEs **16.3%**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Against RTOG 9111 (cisplatin+RT), 2y LFS was **65.1% vs 64.9%** and 2y OS 74.4% vs 74%. Against GORTEC 2000-01 (TPF induction/RT), larynx preservation was **86% vs 75.8%** and larynx dysfunction-free survival 83.7% vs 70.3%. All comparisons are cross-trial.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents newly diagnosed stage III-IVB glottic/supraglottic SCC treated with larynx-preservation intent. Does not represent hypopharyngeal or other head-neck subsites, or pts outside a cisplatin-free trial setting.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The 80% CI is permissive for a 43-pt trial. The case for the regimen rests on **fewer late cisplatin/RT events**, which a 2y analysis cannot yet measure. The RT prescription is not stated in source.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The early oncologic and functional numbers match the cisplatin-RT benchmark without concurrent chemotherapy, so testing whether cisplatin can be replaced is a reasonable next step. Whether the trade of immune toxicity for cisplatin late effects nets out in pts' favor needs longer follow-up and a randomized comparator.

studies.interpretation:
The question SMART-KEY asks is not whether larynx preservation works, but whether it can be achieved without cisplatin, and the trial's own framing makes that clear: standard preservation strategies converge on similar laryngectomy-free survival with no OS separation, so the open problem is late toxicity and non-cancer mortality attributed to concurrent cisplatin with RT. Read that way, the result is meant to show non-inferiority on early outcomes while removing the drug thought to drive late harm. The 2y LFS of 65.1% sitting beside RTOG 9111's 64.9%, and OS 74.4% beside 74%, is about as close as a historical comparison can get, and the proportion alive with a larynx tracks almost exactly.

That closeness should be read with the limits of historical controls in mind. RTOG 9111 enrolled in a different era of staging, imaging, RT technique and supportive care, so a modern single-arm cohort treated with IMRT matching it is partly expected even if the novel components add nothing. The comparison with GORTEC 2000-01 looks more favorable on larynx preservation (86% vs 75.8%) and larynx dysfunction-free survival (83.7% vs 70.3%), but GORTEC used a different induction backbone and a different end-of-induction decision rule. The investigators' wording of "potentially superior" is about as far as the data can carry that point. With 43 pts and an 80% CI of 54.9 to 73.5, the interval comfortably includes LFS meaningfully worse than the cisplatin benchmark.

For an RT reader, the pattern of failure is the useful signal. Locoregional recurrence at 18.8% at 2y against distant recurrence at 7.4% says this approach still fails mainly in the field. That matters because the concurrent phase here is RT plus pembrolizumab alone, so local control depends on RT without a radiosensitizing cytotoxic. The source does not give dose, fractionation or target volumes, which is a real gap: without them a reader cannot tell whether any shortfall in local control should be blamed on removing cisplatin or on the RT prescription, or whether the result transfers to their own institutional practice.

The toxicity trade also deserves more weight than the "well-tolerated" summary suggests. A G≥3 TRAE rate of 41.9%, one treatment-related death and immune-mediated G≥3 events in 16.3% are not trivial for a curative-intent preservation strategy. The regimen also commits pts to roughly a year of consolidation. The premise is that immune toxicity, mostly acute and manageable, is a better bargain than cisplatin's late dysphagia, aspiration and non-cancer mortality. That premise is plausible but untested, and 2y follow-up cannot address it, since late cisplatin-RT harm emerges well beyond that window.

What would make this wrong: a randomized comparison against cisplatin-RT showing inferior local control, or late follow-up showing no reduction in late morbidity or non-cancer death. Until then, SMART-KEY establishes that a cisplatin-free, IO-based preservation pathway is feasible and does not obviously lose early oncologic ground, which justifies a comparative trial rather than a change in practice.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The concurrent phase drops cisplatin, with IMRT given alongside pembrolizumab alone, and 2y larynx preservation was 86%. Locoregional recurrence at 18.8% exceeds distant at 7.4%, so in-field control remains the failure mode to watch; RT dose and volumes are not reported in source.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Carboplatin/paclitaxel/pembrolizumab induction plus 14 cycles of pembrolizumab consolidation replaces cisplatin, with 2y distant recurrence 7.4%. The cost is immune-mediated G≥3 TRAEs in 16.3% and one G5 event, which offsets some of the gain from avoiding cisplatin's late toxicity.

open_questions: Does cisplatin-free IO strategy reduce late morbidity and non-cancer mortality?
Randomized comparison against cisplatin-RT for larynx preservation
RT dose and volumes needed with pembrolizumab-only concurrent therapy

studies.name: KEYNOTE-412 ctDNA analysis
studies.tldr: Mid-CRT (C3D1) ctDNA clearance tracked EFS in HPV- LA HNSCC in both arms; baseline ctDNA was prognostic in HPV- but not HPV+ pts.
details: 🔍 Retrospective ctDNA analysis of phase 3 KEYNOTE-412: pembro or pbo + concurrent CRT, newly diagnosed unresected LA HNSCC
🔍 Tumor-informed Natera Signatera 16-plex; HPV status by p16
🔍 473/804 pts evaluable at both BL and C3D1 (pembro n = 233; pbo n = 240)
🔍 C3D1 drawn in pts who completed 5 of 6-7 wk of CRT, so a mid-RT timepoint
📊 BL ctDNA positivity 95.6% HPV+, 95.3% HPV-
📊 BL ctDNA correlated with BL target lesion size (Spearman ρ = 0.49 HPV-, 0.34 HPV+)
📊 HPV-: higher BL ctDNA → worse OS (pembro arm), worse EFS and OS (pbo arm), P < 0.05
📊 HPV+: no BL ctDNA association with outcome in either arm (P > 0.05)

details.text: 📊 C3D1 ctDNA clearance rate by arm and HPV status
📐 C3D1 clearance vs outcome (P values only; no HRs reported in source)

details: ⚠️ No effect size reported in source: P values only, no HR or absolute EFS/OS by ctDNA group
⚠️ HPV- BL association was dependent on tumor size and stage, so ctDNA may not add beyond TNM
⚠️ Landmark at C3D1 restricted to pts completing CRT; dropouts excluded from the clearance analysis
⚠️ Many arm × HPV × endpoint tests; the HPV+ pbo-only signal is hypothesis-generating

verdict.rationale: Retrospective biomarker analysis of a 59% evaluable subset; P values without HRs, many subgroup tests, and a landmark conditional on completing CRT.
verdict.audience: Newly diagnosed unresected LA HNSCC on definitive CRT

studies.significance: The ctDNA draw at C3D1 falls after 5 of 6-7 wk of CRT, so clearance is effectively a mid-RT response read. In HPV- pts it tracked EFS in both arms (P = 0.001 and 0.011), the signal an adaptive escalation trial would need. Baseline ctDNA carried no prognostic value in HPV+ pts, so it cannot yet select HPV+ pts for de-escalation.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Retrospective ctDNA analysis within phase 3 KEYNOTE-412 (pembro vs pbo + concurrent CRT). Associations tested by **Cox regression**, per arm and by HPV status.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Newly diagnosed, unresected LA HNSCC**. **473 of 804** pts had evaluable ctDNA at both BL and C3D1 (pembro n = 233, pbo n = 240).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Concurrent CRT backbone in both arms; dose and fractionation not reported in source. C3D1 sampled in pts who completed **5 of 6-7 wk of CRT**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: EFS and OS by BL ctDNA level and by C3D1 ctDNA clearance, with HPV by p16.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: BL ctDNA prognostic **only in HPV-** pts (P < 0.05), and not independent of tumor size and stage. Clearance rates were higher with pembro in both HPV strata.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The parent KEYNOTE-412 comparison of pembro + CRT vs pbo + CRT is the context, but its efficacy result is not reported in this source. This is a tumor-informed assay, distinct from the HPV-specific circulating DNA approaches used in HPV+ oropharynx.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents LA HNSCC treated with definitive CRT ± pembro who completed most of CRT. Does not represent resected disease, pts who stopped CRT early, or pts without evaluable samples.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: No HRs or absolute rates, so magnitude is unknown. The HPV- baseline signal depended on tumor size and stage, raising the question of added value over stage.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Mid-CRT clearance looks like a candidate response marker in HPV- disease. It does not settle whether ctDNA-guided intensification or de-escalation changes outcome, and HPV+ results are inconsistent across arms.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: C3D1 falls after 5 of 6-7 wk of CRT, so clearance is a mid-RT response read. In HPV- pts it tracked EFS in both arms (P = 0.001, 0.011), which supports testing ctDNA-adapted escalation. Baseline ctDNA failed in HPV+ pts, so it cannot yet guide RT de-escalation there.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Pembro raised C3D1 clearance in both HPV strata (72.6% vs 63.6% HPV-, 76.8% vs 62.7% HPV+). Clearance tied to OS only in the pembro arm for HPV- pts (P < 0.001), so ctDNA may read IO benefit differently by HPV status. No HRs were given to size that effect.

open_questions: Does ctDNA-guided intensification after mid-CRT non-clearance improve EFS in HPV- disease?
Why is HPV+ clearance prognostic only in the placebo arm?
Does baseline ctDNA add prognostic value beyond tumor size and stage?

studies.name: RADIANT
studies.tldr: RT foundation model: GTV Dice 83.52%, CTV 81.53%; external C-index 0.73-0.79 OS, 0.76-0.86 LC/LRC across lung, oesophageal, rectal, cervical cancers.
details: 🔍 3D Swin Transformer encoder, masked-autoencoder pretraining on 119,782 RT cases from 14 centres
🔍 Inputs paired: planning CT, RT structure sets, 3D dose distributions
🔍 Encoder refined via hierarchical GTV/CTV segmentation plus dose generation
🔍 Hold-out test set: 22,058 cases, 10 most prevalent tumour sites

details.text: 📊 Downstream prediction in independent validation (frozen encoder + generated-dose branch, 21 endpoints)

details: 🔗 Reported to outperform state-of-the-art baselines, especially in external cohorts; baseline metrics not given in source
🔍 Validation cohorts: China, US, Netherlands; retrospective and prospective
⚠️ Discrimination only: no calibration, no clinician-in-loop contour or plan acceptability data reported
⚠️ Dice of 81-84% leaves room for clinically meaningful target edits; no per-site breakdown in source
⚠️ Grad-CAM and transcriptomic findings exploratory; abstract-only source

verdict.rationale: Model development with discrimination metrics only; no prospective test of clinical utility, plan quality, or decision impact. Abstract-only, baseline comparators unquantified.
verdict.audience: Lung, oesophageal, rectal, cervical cancer pts receiving RT

studies.significance: The RT-relevant signal is toxicity and local control: AUC 0.78-0.81 for radiation pneumonitis, 0.84-0.85 for rectal proctitis, and LC/LRC C-index 0.76-0.86, all from a dose-aware encoder. If calibration holds, this informs dose-constraint and de-escalation decisions at planning, but auto-contour acceptability and plan-quality endpoints are absent from source.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Foundation model: 3D Swin Transformer pretrained by masked autoencoding on **119,782** RT cases from **14 centres**, refined with GTV/CTV segmentation and dose generation. Hold-out test **22,058** cases across the 10 most prevalent tumour sites.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Contour Dice, dose-generation errors (ΔHI, ΔD98, ΔD2, ΔDmax, ΔDmean), and **21 downstream endpoints** across lung, oesophageal, rectal and cervical cancers: pCR/response, OS, PFS, LC and RT-related toxicities.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Model ingests planning CT, structure sets and 3D dose; downstream heads add a **generated-dose branch**, so toxicity prediction is dose-informed rather than CT-only.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents RT pts with lung, oesophageal, rectal or cervical cancer across Chinese, US and Dutch cohorts. Does not represent other tumour sites for outcome prediction, or any setting where the model has been tested for clinical decision impact.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Baseline model performance not quantified in source. No calibration, decision-curve, or contour-acceptability data; training skewed to 14 centres, so Western-cohort transfer rests on unstated external sample sizes.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Unifying segmentation, dose generation and outcome prediction in one encoder is the claim; the numbers support discrimination, not workflow readiness. The open step is a prospective test of whether predicted pneumonitis or proctitis risk changes planning.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Dose-aware toxicity prediction is the actionable piece: AUC 0.78-0.81 for radiation pneumonitis and 0.84-0.85 for rectal proctitis, with LC/LRC C-index 0.76-0.86. Plan-level adaptation from these risks is untested; auto-contour Dice 83.52% GTV still implies physician review.

open_questions: Does model-predicted toxicity risk change planning or dose constraints prospectively?
Calibration and performance per tumour site in external cohorts
Clinician acceptability of auto-generated contours and dose

papers.title: RADIANT: A radiotherapy foundation model for treatment planning and outcome prediction across cancers
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 170O · Proffered paper: AI and digital health · 2026-10-24 · presented by Zhen Zhang (Hangzhou, China)

Background: Radiotherapy generates structured planning CT, target/OAR contours and 3D dose maps, yet current AI tools are usually single-task models trained in limited cohorts. We developed RADIANT, a radiotherapy foundation model for an automated workflow from target delineation and dose generation to clinical risk prediction.
Methods: RADIANT used a 3D Swin Transformer encoder pretrained by masked autoencoding on 119,782 radiotherapy cases from 14 centres with paired planning CT, RT structure sets and 3D dose distributions. The encoder was refined with hierarchical GTV/CTV segmentation and dose generation. Outputs were tested in a hold-out set of 22,058 cases from the 10 most prevalent tumour sites. For downstream adaptation, a frozen RADIANT encoder was integrated with a generated-dose branch and task-specific heads for 21 endpoints across lung, oesophageal, rectal and cervical cancers. Validation included retrospective and prospective cohorts from China, the United States and the Netherlands, covering pCR/response, OS, PFS, LC and radiotherapy-related toxicities. Performance was compared with state-of-the-art baseline models.
Results: In hold-out testing, RADIANT achieved overall Dice scores of 83.52% for GTV and 81.53% for CTV, with dose-generation errors of 0.0695 for ΔHI, 0.0706 for ΔD98, 0.0129 for ΔD2, 0.0012 for ΔDmax and 0.0371 for ΔDmean. Across independent validations, RADIANT achieved AUCs of 0.72 for pCR after oesophageal nICT, 0.84 for rectal complete response, 0.78-0.81 for radiation pneumonitis, 0.84-0.85 for rectal radiation proctitis and 0.84 for cervical radiation proctitis. Survival models yielded external C-indices of 0.73-0.79 for OS, 0.71-0.78 for PFS and 0.76-0.86 for LC/LRC. RADIANT consistently outperformed baseline models, particularly in external cohorts. Grad-CAM highlighted clinically plausible tumour and normal-tissue dose interfaces; exploratory transcriptomic analyses suggested biological differences between model-defined risk groups.
Conclusions: Prospective and international multi-centre validation supports RADIANT as a scalable framework for AI-assisted radiotherapy workflows and decision-making.

papers.title: A phase II trial of neoadjuvant nivolumab, docetaxel, and cisplatin followed by surgery and radiation therapy for resectable high-grade salivary gland carcinoma
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1540RO · Rapid oral: Head and neck cancer · 2026-10-25 · presented by Sehhoon Park (Seoul, Republic of Korea) · NCT05727410

Background: Resectable high-grade salivary gland carcinoma (SGC) with clinical node metastasis carries a high risk of distant metastasis despite curative surgery and adjuvant radiotherapy, and effective neoadjuvant strategies remain undefined. We evaluated neoadjuvant nivolumab plus docetaxel and cisplatin (NivoDP) in this aggressive disease.
Methods: This phase II, single-center, single-arm trial enrolled treatment-naïve patients with resectable high-grade SGC and clinically positive lymph nodes. Patients received 3 cycles of nivolumab (360 mg) plus docetaxel (60 mg/m2) and cisplatin (60 mg/m2) q3w, followed by curative surgery and risk-adapted adjuvant radiotherapy. The primary endpoint was major pathologic response (MPR; ≤10% viable tumor).
Results: Of 55 enrolled, 4 screen failures and 1 with benign histology were excluded, leaving 50 analyzed (median age 62; 88.0% male; ECOG 0/1: 12.0%/88.0%). AJCC 8th stage was III/IVA/IVB in 34.0%/64.0%/2.0%. Salivary duct carcinoma predominated (74.0%), followed by adenocarcinoma (10.0%) and mucoepidermoid carcinoma (8.0%). ORR was 52.0%. Forty-six patients underwent surgery (92.0%); 4 did not (1 withdrawal, 2 progression, 1 G3 drug-induced pneumonitis). Among 46 operated patients, R0 resection was 93.5%, MPR 60.9% (n=28), and pCR 32.6% (n=15), exceeding the predefined threshold (MPR ≥50%). Among pathology subtypes, salivary duct carcinoma (MPR 67.6%, pCR 29.4%), adenocarcinoma (MPR 75.0%, pCR 75.0%), and poorly differentiated carcinoma (MPR 66.7%, pCR 66.7%) showed the best response to NivoDP. With a median follow-up of 16.2 months (95% CI 12.0–20.1) from surgery, 12- and 24-month DFS were 89.0% and 76.0%, and 24-month OS 91.2%. The MPR subgroup showed significantly longer DFS than non-MPR (NR vs 24.2 mo; HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05–0.71, p=0.013). Most TRAEs were grade 1–2; 6 grade ≥3 TRAEs were observed, which were all manageable with no treatment-related deaths.
Conclusions: Neoadjuvant NivoDP showed promising clinical efficacy in node-positive high-grade SGC, with high MPR and pCR rates. MPR strongly predicted superior DFS. These results support neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy as a promising strategy in resectable high-grade SGC.
Clinical trial identification: NCT05727410.

papers.title: First interim safety analysis of GORTEC 2024-03 IDEAL: Randomized phase II trial of induction treatment anti–PD-1 pucotenlimab (HX008) plus EGFR-ADC (becotatug vedotin (MRG003) versus EGFR-ADC alone followed by chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1538RO · Rapid oral: Head and neck cancer · 2026-10-25 · presented by Yungan Tao (Villejuif, France) · NCT06959108

Background: The EGFR-directed ADC becotatug vedotin (MRG003) alone or combined with anti-PD1 pucotenlimab (HX008) have shown promising efficacy along with a good safety profile in R/M HNSCC (Xue, Clin. Cancer Res. 2026). The IDEAL trial evaluates induction becotatug vedotin ± pucotenlimab prior to definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in locally advanced (LA) HNSCC.
Methods: Patients (pts) with LA-HNSCC (larynx, hypopharynx, oral cavity, and oropharynx [p16 - and p16 +]) were randomized (1:1) to 2 arms: (A) induction pucotenlimab (200 mg) + becotatug vedotin (2.3 mg/kg) Q3W ×3 → CRT → adjuvant pucotenlimab (Q3W ×8), or (B) induction ADC alone → CRT. CRT consisted of IMRT (70 Gy) + concurrent cisplatin. Primary endpoint is complete response (CR) at 12 weeks post-CRT. Each arm is evaluated independently (one-stage Fleming design; H0=30%). A total of 106 pts is planned. The first interim safety analysis was conducted after completion of cycle 1 in first 20 pts.
Results: Between October 23rd 2025 and April 21st 2026, 49 pts were randomized. Most had oropharyngeal cancer (31 pts, including 19 p16 +). 20 patients (10 per arm) were evaluated for first safety analysis. One death occurred in Arm B (post-gastrostomy, after 1 cycle ADC), deemed unrelated to study treatment. No grade 4 adverse events (AEs) were observed in either arm. A total of 11 Grade 3 TEAEs were observed in 8 pts (6 arm A and 2 arm B). In arm A, these G3 TEAEs were ALT increase + constipation (1 pt), myalgia + ALT increase + hypertension (1), neutropenia (1), diabetes (1), diarrhea (1) and hyponatremia (1). In Arm B, G3 TEAEs were peripheral arterial ischemia (1) and fatigue (1). Data on ORR (per RECIST 1.1) after induction are preliminary and not mature, but ORR observed in 71% of first 15 evaluable pts. Updated safety and post-induction ORR data will be presented at the meeting along with preliminary results on primary endpoint.
Conclusions: First results of induction becotatug vedotin ± pucotenlimab in LA-SCCHN are encouraging and a favorable safety profile was observed.
Clinical trial identification: NCT06959108 First Submitted: 2025-04-28, EU CT 2023-510558-18-00.

papers.title: A single-arm, multi-institutional, phase 2 study of a pembrolizumab-based organ preservation strategy for locally advanced larynx cancers: SMART-KEY (LACOG 0720)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1537RO · Rapid oral: Head and neck cancer · 2026-10-25 · presented by Thiago B. Oliveira (Sao Paulo, Brazil) · NCT04943445

Background: Standard larynx-preserving strategies yield similar laryngectomy-free survival (LFS) with no overall survival (OS) difference, but data raise concerns about late-onset toxicity and mortality, especially for concurrent cisplatin/radiation therapy (RT). We evaluated the addition of pembrolizumab to a cisplatin-free induction, concurrent and consolidation strategy for larynx-preservation.
Methods: This multicenter, single-arm phase 2 trial enrolled patients (pts) with newly diagnosed stage III–IVB glottic/supraglottic squamous cell carcinomas. Pts received induction carboplatin AUC6, paclitaxel 175 mg/m2, and pembrolizumab 200 mg (three 21-day cycles), followed by IMRT with pembrolizumab alone and fourteen 21-day cycles of pembrolizumab consolidation. Primary endpoint was two-year (2y) LFS.
Results: From Feb 2022 to Aug 2023, 43 pts from 9 centers were enrolled (median age 61.1y, 86% male, 74.4% White, 25.6% Black/Mixed, 83.7% former/current smokers, 62.8% glottic). The 2y LFS was 65.1% (80% CI: 54.9-73.5), which compares favorably with historical pivotal trials results. Additional outcomes are presented in the Table. Two-year cumulative incidence of locoregional and distant recurrence were 18.8% and 7.4%. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 41.9% pts (one pt with grade 5), with immune-mediated grade ≥3 TRAEs in 16.3%. Table: 1537RO Outcomes SMART-KEY Historical Control RTOG 9111 (Cisplatin+RT) Historical Control GORTEC 2000-01 (cisplatin, docetaxel, 5-fluorouracil/RT) 2y laryngectomy-free survival 65.1% 64.9% NE 2y larynx preservation rates 86% 88% 75.8% 2y larynx dysfunction-free survival 83.7% NE 70.3% 2y overall survival 74.4% 74% 73% Proportion of pts Alive with larynx 65.1% 64.9% NE Alive after laryngectomy 9.3% 9.1% NE Dead after laryngectomy 4.7% 2.9% NE Dead no laryngectomy 20.9% 23.1% NE
Conclusions: SMART-KEY demonstrated short-term oncological/functional outcomes numerically comparable to RTOG-9111 and potentially superior to GORTEC 2000-01, pivotal trials using cisplatin-based regimens. Our well-tolerated cisplatin-free, concurrent chemotherapy-free strategy also yielded low rates of distant recurrence. The long-term benefit of this regimen will be evaluated with additional follow-up but may have the potential to mitigate cisplatin/RT-related late morbidity/mortality.
Clinical trial identification: NCT04943445.

papers.title: ctDNA analysis of the phase 3 KEYNOTE-412 trial: Pembrolizumab (pembro) or placebo (pbo) + concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA HNSCC)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1536RO · Rapid oral: Head and neck cancer · 2026-10-25 · presented by Jean-Pascal Machiels (Woluwe-Saint-Lambert, Belgium) · NCT03040999

Background: ctDNA is an emerging biomarker in multiple solid tumor types, but its value in LA HNSCC is unclear. KEYNOTE-412 (NCT03040999) evaluated pembro + CRT vs pbo + CRT in participants (pts) with newly diagnosed, unresected LA HNSCC. We retrospectively assessed the association of clinical outcomes with pretreatment ctDNA (baseline [BL] ctDNA) and early on-treatment ctDNA (cycle 3 day 1 [C3D1] ctDNA in pts who completed 5 of 6-7 wk of CRT) in KEYNOTE-412.
Methods: The tumor-informed Natera Signatera 16-plex assay was used to evaluate ctDNA levels in treated pts. Association of BL ctDNA levels and C3D1 ctDNA clearance with EFS and OS were assessed in each arm and by HPV status (by p16 testing) per Cox proportional hazards regression.
Results: Of 804 pts, 473 (pembro arm n = 233; pbo arm n = 240) had evaluable ctDNA samples at both BL and C3D1. BL ctDNA positivity rate was 95.6% for HPV+ and 95.3% for HPV- pts. BL ctDNA levels were positively correlated with BL target lesion size in both HPV- and HPV+ pts (Spearman ρ = 0.49 and 0.34, respectively). Higher BL ctDNA levels were associated with worse OS in the pembro arm and worse EFS and OS in the pbo arm in HPV- pts (P < 0.05); no associations in either arm were observed in HPV+ pts (P > 0.05). The association of BL ctDNA levels with outcomes in HPV- pts was independent of ECOG PS but dependent on tumor size and stage. ctDNA clearance rate at C3D1 was higher in the pembro arm (HPV- 72.6%; HPV+ 76.8%) vs pbo arm (HPV- 63.6%; HPV+ 62.7%). In HPV- pts, ctDNA clearance at C3D1 was associated with improved EFS in both arms (pembro P = 0.001; pbo P = 0.011) and with improved OS in the pembro arm (P < 0.001) but not in the pbo arm (P = 0.075). In HPV+ pts, ctDNA clearance at C3D1 was associated with improved EFS (P = 0.028) and OS (P = 0.013) only in the pbo arm.
Conclusions: The prognostic value of BL ctDNA was observed in HPV- pts with LA HNSCC but not in HPV+ pts. In HPV- pts, a stronger link between C3D1 ctDNA clearance and long-term survival was observed in the pembro arm. These findings suggest distinct ctDNA prognostic values in HNSCC based on HPV status, and long-term outcome associations may differ by treatment modality.
Clinical trial identification: NCT03040999.
